questions.question: Summarize the discussion about setting up the recording equipment
questions.reference_answer: One of the graduate students is working on building the PDA of the future. The idea is to be able to record meetings for personal use and then query them for pertinent information. The data collection will be anonymized to a large extent, but not so much that the meeting does not represent a real scenario. This meeting will be one of the recorded meetings.

oracle.answer: The discussion about setting up the recording equipment primarily revolves around the use of wireless microphones and ensuring they are functioning correctly. Grad A instructs participants to ensure their wireless microphones are on and positioned correctly (about two thumb widths away from the mouth) to minimize breath sounds. They also mention checking the audio levels by observing the little bars that change when speaking. Additionally, Grad A notes that the room is equipped with both tabletop microphones and close-talking microphones to capture high-quality audio for various research purposes, including speech recognition and language analysis. The setup includes simultaneous recording of multiple channels to facilitate tasks such as beam-forming.

A also mentioned that people will be anonymized in the transcript. A explained that the goal was to eventually be able to query meetings for information.

questions.question: Summarize the discussion about the experimental setup of the computer navigation system
questions.reference_answer: The computer navigation system will work as follows. The subject of the experiment will familiarize themselves with information about a city. Then, they will be introduced to an advanced navigation system through which they can navigate the city, and they will be given several tasks, like buying stamps. The navigation system will crash, and the subject will be connected to a human operator. Then, the human operator will control the system based on the subject's requests as the subject tries to complete their tasks. Both sides, the assistant and the subject, will be recorded for data collection purposes.

oracle.answer: The experimental setup for the computer navigation system involves participants reading a text about Heidelberg to familiarize themselves with the area. Participants are then presented with a 3D model or QuickTime animation of Heidelberg and given tasks to complete using a computer system that supposedly understands their queries. Tasks include finding locations, taking pictures, and getting historical information. After completing three tasks, the system crashes, and a human operator takes over to continue the tasks with different objectives. The setup includes a 2D map display showing the participant's location via GPS (which fails after the crash). The experiment records interactions between participants and the system/operator to gather data on how participants interact with the navigation system.

questions.question: What did B think about the experimental setup of the computer navigation system?
questions.reference_answer: B explained that the subject of the experiment will first be given texts about a city, so they can familiarize themselves with foreign terms. Then, they will be introduced to a computer navigation system with which they can navigate the city and provided with a set of tasks to complete. Then, the computer system will crash, including the GPS, so the person will not even know where they are, and the human operator will assist them. To find their location, the subject will have to provide visual information to the human operator. B also thought that creating movies of walking would require a lot of technical effort but later claimed that it may be worth it. B clarified that the goal was to see how people communicate in such a scenario.

The subject then interacts with a computer system to complete tasks such as finding locations and taking pictures, all while the system supposedly knows their location via GPS. After completing several tasks, the system crashes, and a human operator takes over, continuing the tasks without knowing the subject's location, requiring the subject to describe their surroundings. Grad B also mentioned that the setup includes a map-type display and recordings of both sides of the interaction, with the wizard (human operator) potentially being instructed on how expressive and talkative they should be. Grad B seemed to think the setup could provide interesting data but acknowledged the possibility that the data might be limited if the interactions were too simplistic.
